name: Colorectal Gross Anatomy, Appendicitis and Anal Sphincters

reference.source: ALGrawany Anatomy & Physiology Made Easy 2026 / Sabiston Surgery 22e
clinicalPearls: Large bowel hallmarks: three teniae coli, haustra, and appendices epiploicae
All three teniae coli converge at the base of the appendix, serving as an absolute anatomical locator
Acute appendicitis begins with lumen obstruction by fecalith or lymphoid hyperplasia, leading to ischemia and perforation
Pectinate (dentate) line divides upper endodermal anal canal from lower ectodermal anal canal
Above dentate line: visceral innervation (painless internal hemorrhoids); below line: somatic pudendal (painful external hemorrhoids)
reference.pathophysiology: The colon absorbs water and electrolytes and compacts feces. Obstruction of the appendiceal lumen raises intraluminal pressure, compromising venous return, which results in mucosal ulceration, bacterial invasion, gangrene, and peritonitis. At the anorectal junction, the dentate line defines crucial developmental, neurovascular, and lymphatic watersheds.
additionalInvestigations: Contrast-enhanced CT abdomen and pelvis for suspected acute appendicitis
Graded-compression abdominal ultrasound in children and pregnant women
Colonoscopy and proctosigmoidoscopy for colorectal luminal evaluation
